summary.text: 爸 means “father” or “papa.” It is analyzed as a compound in which 父 contributes the father meaning and 巴 supplies a sound cue.

formation.text: The proposed formation is phonosemantic: 父 contributes meaning and 巴 a sound cue. In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, 巴 is reconstructed as *praː and 爸 as *praːs, supporting a sound comparison. The analysis remains qualified because 巴’s early identity and original referent are disputed.

components.text: 父 contributes the meaning “father.” A transmitted Shuowen account describes 父 as a family head holding a staff, but that does not make it a picture of a staff-bearing person within 爸. The selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 父 alone, not an early form of 爸.

巴 is proposed as the sound component. The Shuowen tradition links it to a giant snake; another proposal reads early forms identified as 巴 as a kneeling person. Neither account settles its original name or referent. The selected oracle-style image is a modern redraw of 巴 alone, with an uncertain period; it does not attest 爸.

sound.text: In Zhengzhang’s Old Chinese system, 巴 *praː is compared with 爸 *praːs. In Modern Mandarin, 巴 bā and 爸 bà are also a current reading pair; neither comparison identifies 巴’s original name or referent.
In Modern Mandarin, 巴 bā is compared with 爸 bà. This current reading pair does not by itself establish the historical sound relationship.

history.text: 爸 is absent from Shuowen. A Guangya entry groups 爸 with 爹 and 㸙 under the gloss “father”; this records use of the word, not when the graph was formed. The selected redraws show 父 and 巴 separately, not earlier forms or a sequence for 爸.

One historical dictionary preserves an account in which 父 was added to a father word written 八八 or 巴巴. A later study instead argues that the father word is phonologically from 父. These competing explanations do not establish how or when the graph was formed.

uncertainties.text: No early inscription or dated sequence of the complete graph shows when 父 and 巴 were combined; the phonosemantic analysis remains a proposed account of its construction.

巴’s early form and referent are disputed: the Shuowen tradition associates it with a giant snake, while another proposal interprets forms identified as 巴 as a kneeling person. Its original name is unsettled, so it cannot independently confirm the proposed sound comparison in 爸.

The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan source for the father word and the claim that 爸 preserves an older pronunciation of 父 are not independently substantiated here. These lexical claims are separate from the proposed 巴 sound component.

senses.period: Three Kingdoms era (reported dating of the Guangya record)
senses.text: A Guangya entry is dated to the Three Kingdoms era and glosses 爸 as “father.” This records use of the word, though it does not provide a dated physical witness for the graph.
Modern references gloss 爸 as “father” and “papa”; no separate historical stage for “papa” is established.

limitations.text: The recorded “father” gloss does not date the graph’s formation, and no chronological development from “father” to “papa” is established.
